summary: MOD Service Report consistency tested end-to-end. Backend 12/12 pytest pass (tests/test_mod_service_report_jan2026.py): BFPO engineer job-sheet.pdf for SVC-00038 returns 200 application/pdf, filename 'Service Report - SVC-00038.pdf', text has Service Report / Customer / Site Address / Engineer / Job No and NO 'Electronic Job Sheet' and NO calibration section; MOD PDF page 1 has 4 images vs 3 for non-MOD (MOD badge drawn); 401 without auth; out-of-territory case (Cyprus SVC-00004) blocked for Gibraltar engineer. BFPO staff lee.somers@pulsefitness.com (TempPass123!) also gets 200 + correct filename. Non-MOD SVC-00026 (iso-demo-org, via owner@isodemo.com) still has TREADMILL CALIBRATION. MOD site fault report: 200 linked issue, 404 TEST_ unlinked issue, 404 other-site issue, 401 no auth, 403/404 non-MOD user. PPM GET /api/svc/ppm/schedules/{id} returns is_mod bool (false for iso schedule; true for a TEST_ schedule whose site_id is the MOD Test Site org). Rendered PDFs visually: MOD badge beside Pulse logo with divider, Customer/Engineer boxes equal height and their outer edges flush with the ref table (85+5+85 = 175mm = ref table). Frontend: MOD site user /pulse → Faults → expanded fault shows 'Service report' button for OPEN linked fault and opens PDF in new tab; hidden for TEST_ unlinked fault; BUT also hidden for RESOLVED linked faults (bug). PPM print HTML (Service Desk → Maintenance → search QA Fire → Print): boxes equal height (134-220px) and outer edges (32/868) align exactly with ref table (32/868); Speed/Incline tables identical widths (368/286/163); all .fx tables table-layout fixed; MOD badge rendered when is_mod true (verified via response patch), absent for non-MOD.

minor.issue: is_mod is computed from db.organizations.find_one({id: site_id or organization_id}); for schedules whose site_id is a db.sites id (all current Service Desk schedules) this lookup returns None, so a MOD customer whose sites live in db.sites would get is_mod=false. Works only when site_id is the MOD site org id. Consider also checking the customer org (s.organization_id) account_type / bfpo flags.

ui_bugs.issue: 'Service report' button is rendered INSIDE the `issue.status !== 'resolved'` Status Actions block (IssueDetailPanel.js ~L1099-1120), so it is hidden for resolved faults — exactly when a completed job's service report matters most. Verified: resolved linked fault bdf587ef... shows 0 buttons, open linked fault 79859fb1... shows 1. Move the button outside the status !== 'resolved' conditional.

design_issues.screen: Service Report header (PDF + PPM HTML) for MOD
issues: Double vertical divider before the MOD badge: the code draws a grey divider line (PDF canvas.line / CSS .imod border-left) and the mod-badge.png artwork already contains its own dark vertical rule, so two lines appear side by side. Drop one.
Footer image max-width 760px is narrower than content width (~836px at 900px window) so footer doesn't align to the right edge on-screen (print is fine).

action_items: Move the mod-fault-service-report-btn out of the `issue.status !== 'resolved'` block in IssueDetailPanel.js so resolved/closed faults with a linked job can download the Service Report
